intro: Adjectives with -ísimo, exclamations with «qué» and «cuánto», and diminutives with -ito.
p.buenísimo.consejo: It comes from «bueno»: the final o is replaced by -ísimo. You do not say «muy buenísimo».
p.riquísimo.consejo: From «rico»: the c becomes qu to keep the k sound.
p.larguísimo.consejo: From «largo»: the g becomes gu to keep the g sound: larguísimo.
p.muchísimo.consejo: «Mucho» + -ísimo. It works with verbs: «me gusta muchísimo».
p.facilísimo.consejo: From «fácil»: it loses the accent and the c sounds th: fa-thi-LI-si-mo.
p.vaya.consejo: With a noun it expresses surprise: «¡Vaya coche!». It is also a form of the verb «ir».
p.cuánta.glosa: how much; what a lot of
p.cuánta.consejo: In exclamations it has an accent and agrees: «¡cuánta gente!», «¡cuántos coches!».
p.cafecito.consejo: From «café» it is formed with -cito, not -ito. It is very common in the Americas.
p.momentito.consejo: From «momento» + -ito. It sounds kind when asking people to wait: «un momentito, por favor».
p.cerquita.consejo: From «cerca»: the c becomes qu to keep the k sound: cerquita.
p.poquito.consejo: From «poco»: the c becomes qu. «Un poquito» softens what you say.
b1.texto:
**-ísimo** gives a very strong degree: caro → **carísimo**, rica → **riquísima**. It agrees with the noun: un café carísimo, unas tapas riquísimas.

Exclamations: **¡Qué** bonito! **¡Qué** día **tan** bonito! **¡Cuánta** gente! **¡Vaya** coche!

The diminutives **-ito / -ita** soften or show affection: un cafecito, un momentito, cerquita.
b2.f6.texto: There is a little café very close to here.
b2.f7.texto: What a lot of people there are in the square!
b4.texto:
**-ísimo:** drop the final vowel and add -ísimo: caro → carísimo, bueno → buenísimo. Some letters change to keep the sound: rico → ri**qu**ísimo, largo → lar**gu**ísimo, feliz → feli**c**ísimo. Do not say «muy carísimo».

**Exclamations:**
- ¡Qué + adjective or noun! ¡Qué calor!
- ¡Qué + noun + tan / más + adjective! ¡Qué día tan bonito!
- ¡Cuánto / cuánta / cuántos / cuántas + noun! ¡Cuánta gente!

**Diminutives:** poco → poquito, café → cafecito, cerca → cerquita.
b4.e2.texto: What a lot of people there are in the square!
b5.f0.texto: The market in the square smells of cinnamon, ripe fruit and freshly baked bread.
b5.f1.texto: The fruit stalls shine like little lamps of colours.
b5.f2.texto: A seller with quick hands piles the oranges into a very tall tower.
b5.f3.texto: Lucía stops in front of a basket full of very sweet figs.
b5.f4.texto: She tastes one and closes her eyes with a huge smile.
b5.f5.texto: Pablo looks at the square full of people and thinks that everything is gorgeous.
b5.f6.texto: A musician plays a very slow waltz on the accordion next to the fountain.
b5.f7.texto: The children run around him with little spoons of ice cream in their hands.
b5.f8.texto: The sun sinks slowly and fills the air with a very soft light.
b5.f9.texto: Marta breathes deeply, opens her arms and says in a very soft voice that she will never forget this afternoon.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! The adjective takes the ending -ísimo.
b6.o1.refuerzo: With -ísimo it is already very strong: «muy» is too much.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The final vowel drops first: caro → carísimo.
b6.pregunta: You want to say «extremely expensive». Which form?
b7.o0.refuerzo: It would be read with th: the c has to become qu.
b7.o1.refuerzo: The final vowel drops first and then -ísimo is added.
b7.o2.refuerzo: That is it! The c becomes qu to keep the k sound.
b9.o0.refuerzo: This exclamation does not use «muy»: the pattern asks for «tan» or «más».
b9.o1.refuerzo: Well done! «Qué día tan bonito» is the pattern.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Before an adjective you say «tan», not «tanto».
b9.pregunta: Qué + noun + ... + adjective. What is missing?
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes! Words ending in a stressed vowel take -cito.
b10.o1.refuerzo: That form does not exist; the usual one is «cafecito».
b10.o2.refuerzo: That form is not used; the usual one is «cafecito».
b10.pregunta: What is the usual diminutive of «café»?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «What a lot of people!»
b12.o0.refuerzo: It is masculine singular, and «tapas» is feminine plural.
b12.o1.refuerzo: It is masculine plural, and «tapas» is feminine.
b12.o2.refuerzo: That is it! It agrees in feminine plural with «tapas».
p.esperad.consejo: Command form of «esperar» for «vosotros». Used mainly in Spain.
p.lámparas.consejo: Plural of «lámpara». The accent marks stress on «LAM».
p.rápidas.consejo: Feminine plural of «rápido», agreeing with «manos». Stress on «RRA».
p.torre.consejo: A tall structure. Between vowels the «rr» is strong.
p.altísima.consejo: Superlative of «alta», with «-ísima». It means extremely tall.
p.cesto.consejo: The «c» before «e» sounds like «th» in Spain.
p.higos.consejo: The «h» is silent, and the «g» before «o» is hard.
p.dulcísimos.consejo: Superlative of «dulces» with «-ísimos». The «c» in «dulce» sounds like «th».
p.bellísimo.consejo: Superlative of «bello», with «-ísimo». The «ll» sounds like «y».
p.músico.consejo: A person who plays music. The accent on «ú» marks stress.
p.vals.consejo: A dance in three beats. The «v» sounds like «b».
p.acordeón.consejo: An instrument with bellows and keys. The accent on «ó» is the stress.
p.cucharitas.consejo: Diminutive of «cuchara». Small spoons, like those for ice cream.
p.suavísima.consejo: Superlative of «suave», with «-ísima». The «v» sounds like «b».
p.olvidará.consejo: Future of «olvidar», for «ella». The accent on «á» marks stress.
p.tapas.consejo: Small dishes shared in Spain. Stress on «TA».
